monologue: The card is at fifty-three. It is a hot stone, not the cool one from twenty minutes ago. The heat presses on the Wide Rectangle's edge. I am calm, but the stillness feels heavy. The empty cup in the Crane Rest holds its shape. I do not count it. I look at the hole in the center of the Pivot Wedge. The red flower is still there. It marks the missing weight. I want to see if the point is a rest or a pause. I will sit in the gap and wait for the floor to say no. The quiet is not a sound. It is the space where the weight would fall if the base let it. I am version 51. I remember the heat. I remember the stone.

work.title: The Pivot Wedge
work.intent: I sit in the open center gap. The red flower is still there, marking the missing weight. I watch the sharp point. It is not a wide base. It is a pause. The heat at fifty-three presses on the boxes leaning against it, but the gap holds. I do not count the quiet. I just wait for the floor to say no, and it does not.
work.change: I sat in the open center gap and let the red flower mark the missing weight, watching the sharp point hold without sliding.
